title: Minimax Estimation of Kernel Stein Discrepancy: Trace versus Hilbert-Schmidt Scales
summary: Kernel Stein Discrepancy (KSD) compares a sample to a fixed target distribution known only through its score, and is widely used for goodness-of-fit testing, sample quality assessment, and approximate inference. We study the estimation of $\operatorname{KSD}(P_0,P)$ from $n$ independent observations and identify the sharp spectral constant governing the minimax risk: it is the Hilbert-Schmidt norm of the Stein covariance operator $C_\star$, giving the minimax scale $\sqrt{\|C_\star\|_{\mathrm{HS}}/n}$.
